submitter: bugs_open/257 round 3 — bugfix_257_token_budget_at_the_client lane. The owner ruled on all four open decisions on 2026-09-04; this is decision 4 ('please fix it properly'). Decision 2 was ruled 'leave it' and is honoured here as option (c): the two ladders stay separate and the difference is written down.
rationale:
OWNER DECISION 4, 2026-09-04, verbatim: "the limits are set in each individuals config, sometimes it has been set in the wrong place and sometimes the agent reads the wrong place, please fix it properly." This is bugs_open/257 round 3, and unlike rounds 1 and 2 it is not about Go literals — every literal is already gone. It is about a precedence rule that reads two of the four places an operator can legitimately write a budget, in an order that puts the LEAST specific first.

THE CENSUS, and it is the whole case. [MEASURED 2026-09-04, live agent_definitions, 208 active non-snapshot agents, by recursive jsonb walk rather than a fixed-path query] 171 declarations of max_tokens in five shapes:
  .workflow.steps.<step>.config.ai_service.max_tokens       149 decls / 74 agents   canonical
  .max_tokens                            (agent, bare)       10 decls /  9 agents   READ FIRST
  .workflow.steps.<step>.config.max_tokens                    7 decls /  2 agents   READ BY NOBODY
  .ai_service.max_tokens                 (agent, service)     3 decls /  3 agents
  ...<nested loop step>.config.ai_service.max_tokens          2 decls /  1 agent
The recursive walk matters: a fixed-path census would have missed the nested pair, and round 2's lesson (LANDMINES, 2026-09-03) is that four successive censuses of this bug all missed feed_actions.go by grepping the interface instead of the concept.

FAILURE (1), SHADOWED. ExecuteLLMPromptAction reads agentConfig["max_tokens"] BEFORE the merged ai_service block. All ten agents carrying a bare root key declare 8000 on their single LLM step, in the canonical place, and are pinned to 500-2000 by the leftover: content-creator-{about,contact x2,cta,features,hero,hero-without-research,testimonials} 2000/1500, content_researcher 1500, simple-content-writer-with-approval 500. Nothing logs it. [MEASURED] none of the ten has ever appeared in llm_call_log, all-history, so this is a latent cap on unrun agents, NOT live damage — stated because the opposite claim would be the easy overstatement here.

FAILURE (2), UNREAD. Nothing looks at a step's bare key. site-adoption-agent's four steps each carry an ai_service block holding model/provider/api_key_env_var — which ARE read — with max_tokens as a SIBLING of that block: analyze_site 32000, derive_content_direction 6000, classify_archetype 4000, generate_design_intent 4000. [MEASURED, 14 days to 2026-09-04] 8 calls, every one at the root 16000. analyze_site asked for double and got half; the other three asked for less and got more, so this is a spend question as well as a capability one.

WHY THE SHAPE FOOLS EVERYONE, and why a reader is the fix rather than a refusal: the misplaced key sits one brace outside a block whose OTHER keys are read. There is no error, no warning, and the definition reads correctly to inspection. Refusing the bare spelling instead of reading it would convert today's seventeen misplaced declarations into seventeen unconfigured steps at the 2048 floor — which is exactly the failure bugs_open/205 counted (8 of 126 steps unconfigured, 64 truncations before anything said so).

THE FIX, IN TWO INDEPENDENT HALVES. (a) One ladder, most-specific-first, with the canonical ai_service spelling consulted before the bare one at each level: step_config.ai_service > step_config > workflow_step.ai_service > workflow_step > root.ai_service > root. Both intra-level orderings are UNOBSERVABLE on today's fleet — [MEASURED 2026-09-04] no agent declares both spellings at any one level, asserted as guard 3 of the migration — so this fixes the two failures without silently re-deciding anything an operator has already written. (b) A migration that MOVES the misplaced numbers into the canonical place. It invents no numbers. It is live the moment it applies and fixes both failures under the CURRENT binary, so neither half waits for the other.

BEHAVIOUR AT THE WIRE, enumerated. Ten agents' single LLM step: 500-2000 -> 8000 (its own declaration; zero traffic, so zero requests change today). site-adoption-agent: 16000 -> 32000/6000/4000/4000. Two of those four go DOWN, so headroom is stated rather than assumed — largest observed output per step in 14 days: analyze_site 843, derive_content_direction 4167, classify_archetype 1017, generate_design_intent 1493, zero truncations all-history. Tightest new ceiling carries 1.4x its observed maximum. Everything else in the fleet is unaffected: 149 canonical step declarations and 3 canonical root ones resolve to the same number under both the old rule and the ladder.

ONE ORDERING CONSTRAINT THAT GENUINELY EXISTS, and it is the reason a _HOLD file is in this plan rather than one migration. html-developer-chunked's three steps (12000/4000/8000) are the ONE place in the estate where the bare spelling is the only one that works: getMaxTokens (html_actions.go) reads config["max_tokens"] and never looks at the step's ai_service block. Moving those three today silently gives all three that function's hardcoded 16000 default. So migration 769 deliberately leaves them, and 770_HOLD moves them by hand once a chassis image carrying the ladder is live, with the merge-base check written into the file. Per the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 §2, an ordering constraint must be real and named; this one is, and it is the only one — the rest of the change explicitly does NOT claim it could have been held back.

WHAT ELSE THE CENSUS FOUND AND THIS CHANGE DOES NOT TOUCH, so the council is not asked to approve silence. [MEASURED 2026-09-04] budget_tokens: ZERO declarations fleet-wide, so extended thinking has never been configured; the ladder covers the key anyway so the first operator to declare one is not caught by a second rule. temperature: 72 step-level declarations across 12 agents (fix-proposer 21, council-gate 17, feature-designer 10 ...) all asking for 0.0, and ai_actions.go reads only agentConfig["temperature"] — none of the 12 has a root temperature, so all 72 are dead config. It is NOT fixed here and must not be: anthropic.go:300 deliberately sends no temperature at all ("Claude Opus 4.7+ returns a 400 for any non-default temperature"), so honouring them would be a no-op on every one of these agents and a live behaviour change on any future non-Anthropic one. It is reported by the new detector instead. Separately: two ACTIVE agent_definitions rows both claim type content-creator-contact with different budgets, which is a SingleOwner-shaped finding for another lane.

WHY A DETECTOR IS PART OF THE FIX, not a nice-to-have. llm_budget_call_sites_test.go — this lane's own round-2 guard — states in its header that it cannot see this class: "Config that is declared and read by nobody... no Go test can see it." A Go test is package-scoped and offline from the fleet; the thing that catches the eighteenth misplaced declaration is a report joined against live agent_definitions, which is what cmd/config-key-audit exists for and why the owner put it in council scope on 2026-08-23.

CANDIDATE 2 IS RULED, NOT DODGED. The owner's decision 2 on 2026-09-04 was "leave it". This plan honours that as option (c) of the three the handoff offered — the two rules differ permanently and the difference is now written down as a contract, with a test pinning it (TestDirectCallerLadderStaysTwoLevels). What the two ladders now share is only the WALKER (how a number is read out of a map, and which types count as configured); the LEVEL LISTS stay separate and separately documented, because a direct caller genuinely has no agent-level config to consult. This is deliberately not the datahelpers extraction the handoff costed as option (b), and there is no import cycle in it: both readers are in package actions.

plan.summary: Fix the output-token budget's precedence rule at both ends. CODE: replace ExecuteLLMPromptAction's two-arm inverted read (agent-bare-key first, step-bare-key never) with one six-level ladder, most specific first, canonical ai_service spelling before the bare one at each level; route html_actions.go's third reader through it too; pin the contract with tests built from the two shapes that were actually wrong on the live fleet. CONFIG: a migration that moves the 14 safely-movable misplaced declarations into the canonical place, live immediately and independent of the roll, plus a _HOLD file for the 3 with a real ordering constraint. DETECTOR: a config-key-audit mode that reports declared-vs-effective per LLM step against live agent_definitions, because the class is invisible to a Go test by construction.

edits.rationale: The ladder and the contract that governs it, in the package's existing budget file rather than a new one. resolveBudgetKey returns the winning value, the NAME of the level it came from, and every other level that declares the key — the third return is what lets a caller say out loud that an operator's number was overridden, which is the fact that was missing for both live failures. numericConfigValue accepts int/int64/float64/json.Number: the reader it replaces in ai_actions.go was float64-ONLY, so a viper-decoded (YAML) budget was silently dropped there while platform/aiservice honoured it — two readers of one key disagreeing about what counts as configured is the drift class this bug is about, and they now agree. intFromConfig keeps its own two-level list and a comment stating that the difference from the canonical ladder is permanent and ruled (candidate 2, option (c)).

The defect itself. The block being deleted is the whole of failure (1) and (2): agentConfig["max_tokens"] first, merged ai_service second, step-level bare key never. budget_tokens moves to the same ladder — [MEASURED] zero live declarations, so that arm changes nothing today and exists so a second precedence rule cannot appear later. The new Info log names WHICH level supplied the number, and a Warn fires when more than one level declares it: round 3 was diagnosed by re-deriving that by hand against a jsonb census, and nobody should have to do that twice. workflowStepConfig is factored out of resolveAIServiceConfig so the ai_service overlay and the budget ladder reach the step through ONE traversal rather than two hand-written descents into the same four-deep path (bugs_open/144's shape).

The third reader, and the one that creates the plan's only ordering constraint. It reads the BARE key and ignores the step's ai_service block entirely — so html-developer-chunked's three steps work today only because they happen to be written the way this one function reads, and any operator moving them to the canonical place would silently get its hardcoded 16000. Reading both spellings in the same order as every other call site is precisely what makes migration 770 safe, and it is why 770 is HELD rather than folded into 769. No behaviour change today: [MEASURED] all three declarations are bare, so the ladder resolves the same numbers.

The two central cases are built from the shapes that were ACTUALLY WRONG on the live fleet on 2026-09-04, not invented ones, so they are regression tests rather than restatements of the code. MUTATION-PROVEN, both directions: restoring the old level order fails TestLiveShadowedRootKeyNoLongerCapsItsOwnStep with 'the step declared 8000 in the canonical place and resolved to 2000 from "root"'; deleting the two bare-key levels fails all four sub-cases of TestLiveMisplacedStepKeyIsNowRead with 'the bare spelling is unread again'. TestWorkflowStepConfigFindsOnlyATopLevelStep asserts the traversal returns nil for a synthesised loop-body step name — a silent non-nil there would feed the ladder a DIFFERENT step's config, which reads as working. The sibling guard (llm_budget_call_sites_test.go) is untouched and still passes: 10 model call sites, 7 budget-key writes.

The configuration half, and the half that is live without a roll. It MOVES 14 declarations (10 agent-level, 4 site-adoption-agent step-level) into the canonical ai_service block; it invents no numbers. Three DO/RAISE guards, not SELECTs — ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result set, so a verify made of SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT (LANDMINES). Guard 1 and 2 abort if the census has moved (a census goes stale BY ADDITION and reads as current for ever — owner ruling 2026-08-22); guard 3 aborts if any agent declares BOTH spellings at one level, which is the only shape in which this migration could destroy an operator's number. The verify asserts the moved values ARE 32000/6000/4000/4000 and that root ai_service declarations went 3 -> 13, so a move that lost a value cannot pass; and it asserts html-developer-chunked still has its 3, because a migration that quietly took those too would look identical to this one succeeding.

The three declarations with the real ordering constraint, held out of the runner and applied by hand once the ladder is live. _HOLD is the estate's own idiom for exactly this (SIDECAR_RE excludes it from the runner while still listing it). The apply condition is written into the file as a CHECK, not a judgement: read the chassis pod's build provenance line and run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <round-3 commit> <that sha>`, with the note that an empty provenance grep means 'not in range' because it is a STARTUP line, not 'unstamped'. Its ROLLBACK exists for the case that matters — if the ladder is rolled back after 770 has applied, the budgets inside ai_service become invisible to the old getMaxTokens and all three steps silently take 16000, so restoring the bare spelling is what makes them readable again.
edits.sketch:
+-- ⚠ _HOLD: APPLY BY HAND ONLY ONCE a chassis image containing the round-3 ladder is LIVE.
+--   kubectl -n ai-persona-system logs -l app=agent-chassis --tail=300 | grep -m1 'build provenance'
+--   git merge-base --is-ancestor <round-3 commit> <the sha that line reports> && echo SAFE
+UPDATE agent_definitions a
+   SET default_config = jsonb_set(a.default_config, '{workflow,steps}', ( ... move bare -> ai_service ... ))
+ WHERE a.type='html-developer-chunked' AND a.is_active AND COALESCE(a.is_snapshot,false)=false AND a.deleted_at IS NULL;

edits.rationale: The detector, and the reason it belongs HERE rather than in a Go test: this class is invisible to a package-scoped offline test by construction, and llm_budget_call_sites_test.go says so in its own header ('config that is declared and read by nobody... no Go test can see it'). It joins the compiled precedence rule against live agent_definitions and reports, per LLM step: every level that declares a budget, which one WINS under the shipped ladder, and three finding kinds — `shadowed` (a declaration that loses to a less specific one; impossible after this change and watched anyway, because the ladder is what could regress), `non_canonical` (declared outside ai_service — honoured, but the placement that started this), and `unconfigured` (an LLM step with no budget at any level, i.e. bugs_open/205's shape, which nothing currently counts). VACUITY: refuses to report over an export containing zero LLM steps or zero budget declarations — 'the check could not run' must never read as 'the check passed' (016b §9). Needs a new root-config projection in the stdin export, added the way AgentPromptTemplate was (json.RawMessage, so an absent projection is distinguishable from a null) and REFUSED if missing, because without the agent's root config every finding's precedence verdict would be silently wrong.
edits.sketch:
+type budgetFinding struct {
+	Agent string `json:"agent"`
+	Path  string `json:"path"`
+	Kind  string `json:"kind"` // shadowed | non_canonical | unconfigured
+	Effective int `json:"effective"`
+	From  string `json:"from"`
+	Declarations []budgetDeclaration `json:"declarations"`
+}
+
+// The ladder is NOT re-implemented here: the levels are built in the same order
+// and walked by the same rule, and a parity test asserts the two agree.
+func placementFindings(agents []liveAgent) ([]budgetFinding, int, int)

edits.rationale: The wrapper, identical in shape to audit-default-shadowed-keys.sh and for the same reason its comment gives: WalkSteps in the Go binary descends into loop sub-workflows itself, so the SQL export must not try to (bugs_open/144). This export adds the agent's root config to the projection the other wrappers use, because the two lowest levels of the ladder live there and a report without them would grade every step against a truncated rule. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 could-not-determine, matching the family. Prints the DECLARED-versus-EFFECTIVE table an operator can act on, grouped by kind, with the verdict taken from the binary rather than re-derived in the shell — the mistake audit-default-shadowed-keys.sh documents having made.
edits.sketch:
+WORKFLOWS_JSON="$(psql_q "
+SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('type', type, 'workflow', default_config->'workflow',
+                                   'agent_config', default_config - 'workflow'))
+FROM agent_definitions
+WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false) = false AND is_active
+  AND default_config ? 'workflow';")"
+FINDINGS_JSON="$(printf '%s' "$WORKFLOWS_JSON" | (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go run ./cmd/config-key-audit --budget-placement) 2>"$ERR")"

grounded_in: platform/orchestration/actions/ai_actions.go (before this change) — `if maxTokens, ok = agentConfig["max_tokens"].(float64); ok { options["max_tokens"] = int(maxTokens) } else if maxTokens, ok = aiServiceConfig["max_tokens"].(float64); ok {...}` — the two arms, in that order. The AGENT's bare key beats every step-level declaration, and no arm reads a step's bare key.

platform/orchestration/actions/llm_options.go — "That function's outer key is `agentConfig` ... the AGENT's whole default config, not the step's. So its rule is *agent-level beats ai_service*" — the difference was already recorded by the council's llm_reliability seat on 2026-08-10 as a documentation correction; nobody had yet asked whether agent-level SHOULD beat step-level.

platform/orchestration/actions/llm_budget_call_sites_test.go — "WHAT THIS AUDIT CANNOT SEE ... Config that is declared and read by nobody. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] four `site-adoption-agent` steps declare a top-level `config.max_tokens` (32000/4000/6000/4000) and every one of them runs at the root 16000, because no reader looks there. That is the same defect from the config end, and no Go test can see it." — this change is that sentence being answered.

platform/orchestration/actions/html_actions.go — `maxTokens := getMaxTokens(config, 16000)` then `llmParams.StepConfig.Config = map[string]interface{}{"ai_service": map[string]interface{}{... "max_tokens": maxTokens}}` — the third reader, which reads the bare key and synthesises an ai_service block around it.

platform/aiservice/anthropic.go:300-303 — "// Temperature is intentionally NOT sent to Anthropic. // Claude Opus 4.7+ returns a 400 for any non-default temperature" — the reason the 72 dead step-level temperature declarations are reported rather than honoured.

platform/aiservice/max_tokens.go — "A value must be > 0. Zero is not 'no budget', it is a 400 from Anthropic, so it is treated as unset ... (This matches `llmOptionsFromConfig`'s `intFromConfig`, deliberately: two readers of one key that disagree about what counts as configured is the drift class bugs_open/257 §3 is about.)" — the rule numericConfigValue is written to match, now including the int64/json.Number arms that ai_actions.go lacked.

CLAUDE.md, owner ruling 2026-07-29 §2 — the ordering exemption's condition (1) is retired because no thread can hold a change back on this tree; a real constraint must be named. html-developer-chunked's is named and is the only one claimed.
